Key Responsibilities

Processes

  • Accurate input of loan transactions in the TP System
  • Ensure all agreed checks in pre- processing / processing are strictly carried out.
  • Accurate processing and follow up of fee related transactions.
  • Ensure zero tolerance areas like Nostro and Suspense reconciliations are done and to date.
  • Support action points / accepted suggestions of Audit teams (QA, CORAM, GIA etc.) are implemented in the work place within the accepted timelines.
  • Ensure mails are responded completely, comprehensively and immediately. In cases where response cannot be prepared immediately, suitable holding response is forwarded with reasonable timelines for completion.
  • Participate in team meetings and ensure implementation of agreed action points.
  • Attend nominated classroom trainings and complete e-learnings on time.
  • Support implementation of key projects.
  • Diarize transactions which needs manual control and ensure action on or before due date.
  • Update control sheet and reconcile the daily instructions.
  • Update productivity and error data correctly.
  • Gain knowledge in system and process and keep up to date.
  • Ensure timely archival of records with service provider and proper maintenance of inventory of archived records.

Risk Management

  • Support CST RP by providing necessary samples/ clarifications.
  • To escalate unit’s OR issues and losses to Manager

Regulatory & Business Conduct

  • Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
  • Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.
  • Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters.

Key Stakeholders

  • Peers, Subordinates, Managers, Senior Managers in GLS, CPC / GBS China
  • Peers in other units in GBS China

Other Responsibilities

  • To actively participate in BCP / DR and any other UAT.
  • Actively participate in Outserve / Ideal Projects and Initiatives
  • Participation in engagement and CSR activities
  • Ensure proper maintenance of work stations and the environment of GLS work place.
  • Ensure adherence of clean desk policy.
  • Embed Here for good and Group’s brand and values in GLS

Skills And Experience

  • Lending product knowledge
  • Data analyse
  • Project management

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor degree and above
  • Certifications: CET-6 and above
  • Languages: Great communication in English (articulation and writing) and very good excel skill

About Standard Chartered

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What We Offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

CIB COO (Corporate and Institutional Banking)

Our COO team delivers strategic execution for Corporate and Institutional Banking (CIB) across the globe. Through transformative data and digital solutions, customer servicing, and non-financial risk expertise, this team is where problems are solved, and careers are made.

CIB COO Focuses On These Key Priorities

  • Protecting the bank, our customers and stakeholders by enhancing our operational resilience, strengthen our control environment, and improve risk management.
  • Driving operational excellence and efficiency by optimising our processes and delivering the transition to net zero in our own operations.
  • Enabling business growth exceptional service by enabling our businesses to focus on our competitive advantage and deliver transformation and digitisation across the bank.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team.

In This Role, You Will

Collect relevant information from various sources to assist the Relationship Managers with facilities related to credit proposals and operational matters

Check covenant compliance certificate and covenant fulfilment

Support Security Control co-ordination

Check facility letters prepared by Credit Ops or Relationship Managers, ensure the return of acknowledged copies of such letters prior to the expiry date therein and take prompt follow-up action on outstanding items

Check customer and facility related documents and take prompt follow-up action on outstanding items. To arrange renewal of security documents

Facilitate the loan drawdown process through close liaison with Client Management and Credit Ops on account opening, and ensure that security requirements have been completed before facilityc limits are loaded

Work closely with CLM and relationship managers in the team and support them to complete all KYC process in a timely manner.

Execute or support the approval of low/medium risk periodic review profile

Reconcile the data in OMNIA and the baseline in DCP report

Deal independently with e-mail or telephone enquiries from customers and liaise closely with other HSBC departments and branches in answering / resolving customer queries / issues. Proactively follow-up on outstanding matters

Undertake all required activities as directed by line manager or as agreed in annual objectives in support of the development of the Banking business

To be successful in the role, you should meet the following requirements:

Solid understanding of Banking operations and its products / services, general knowledge of trade, treasury, and payment and cash management products and activities

Relevant work experience supporting Relationship Managers or Sales teams in a financial institution (bank or non-bank)

Relevant credit application and credit monitoring experience is a plus

Excellent client servicing skills (minimum 2 years of service in a client facing role)

Results focused and an ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-moving environment

Ability to work independently but also as a team player, with highly developed interpersonal skills

Ability to prioritize competing demands

Ability to understand and consolidate diverse and complex business information and identify and mitigate risk issues

Be change oriented and explore ways of enhanced working and have a forward-thinking mind-set, in line with the Group's values and strategy

Excellent analysis and problem-solving skills

Proficient in AI tools

Fluent verbal and written English

You’ll achieve more at HSBC.

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within and inclusive and diverse environment. Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

Issued by HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited

Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking is a leading global financial institution that provides advisory, investment banking, financing, corporate banking and capital markets services to corporations, financial institutions, financial sponsors and sovereign and supranational organizations worldwide.

  • Good command in English and Chinese, both written and oral

HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking(CIB)

HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking is a markets-led, financing-focused business that provides investment and financial solutions. Through our international network, we connect emerging and mature markets, covering key growth areas. We partner with our corporate, government and institutional clients to help them achieve consistent, long-term performance. Our products and services include advisory, financing, prime services, research and analysis, securities services, trading and sales and transaction banking.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team.

In This Role, You Will

This role is responsible for supporting origination, structuring, and execution of complex financing transactions for both corporate and sponsor clients, including but not limited to syndicated loans and acquisition finance, while maintaining a strict adherence to risk management and regulatory compliance standards.

Business

  • Support the origination, structuring, and execution of complex financing solutions for both corporate and sponsor clients, and assist with distribution if applicable
  • End-to-end transaction execution, from preparing pitching materials, assistance in credit proposal to preparing transactional documents under senior guidance
  • Supporting credit analysis to assess risk and structure appropriate financing solutions
  • Contribute to the achievement against team's targets for revenue generation, product alignment, customer satisfaction, cost management etc.
  • Contribution to the growth of HSBC's share of client wallet
  • Ensure strict adherence to internal risk management frameworks, credit policies, and regulatory compliance standards through all stages of transaction process
  • Collaborate closely with relevant stakeholders
  • Champion a culture of compliance and ethical conduct within the team, ensuring all activities align with the Bank's regulatory obligations and internal governance standards

Customers and Stakeholders

  • Support the engagement with various stakeholders including Coverage, Risk, RC, Legal and others as required to ensure smooth executional service is provided to clients and internal parties
  • Deliver the best-in-class client experience by embracing a collaborative and inclusive culture and forward-looking mindset

To be successful in the role, you should meet the following requirements:

  • Credit sense, financial modelling skills, along with a high level of attention to details
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to thrive in a high-pressure environment and manage multiple live transactions simultaneously
  • Self-motivation with strong willingness to learn and explore outside comfort zone

You’ll achieve more at HSBC.

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within and inclusive and diverse environment. Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

We work in an agile manner and at pace, partnering with teams in Technology and Digital Business Services to bring innovative, digital-first solutions to our customers.

Some careers have more impact than others.

If you’re looking for a career where you can make a real impression, join HSBC and discover how valued you’ll be.

HSBC is one of the largest banking and financial services organisations in the world, with operations in 64 countries and territories. We aim to be where the growth is, enabling businesses to thrive and economies to prosper, and, ultimately, helping people to fulfil their hopes and realise their ambitions.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of Manager, Regulatory Risk.

Principal responsibilities

The purpose of this role is to oversee key regulatory risk initiatives including the Regulatory Runway, compliance to internal and external policies (e.g. Conflict of Interest, Information Control, etc) and AB&C Compliance across IWPB Asia

  • Drive the implementation of global policies and procedures across ASP markets (e.g. AB&C, Conflict of Interest (GPAD), Information Control, Volcker, High Risk Role framework etc) and provide advisory guidance/ act as a subject matter expert to markets as needed.
  • Proactively engage with key stakeholders (e.g. first and second line of defense and Audit) to understand and resolve risks and issues.
  • Manage the implementation of key de-risking programs and support special BRR projects to mitigate the emerging risks as they arise.
  • Continue to improve the effectiveness and efficiency on how IWPB manage regulatory risk and controls.
  • Ensure efficient policy rollout and quality implementation of external regulatory changes in a timely manner by mobilising resources at the regional and market level.
  • Monitor the current and emerging risk and control environment. Lead risk read across initiatives and provide updates and escalation to senior management as needed.
  • Interpret regulations and Policy with the support of risk stewards and anticipate key problems and drive solutions. Provide policy related clarifications to markets to enable alignment across the region. Provide feedback to policy owners for possible improvements to policies.
  • Facilitate the FIM dispensation process by reviewing and recommending appropriate response to Senior Management and obtaining business approval for IWPB markets in the region.
  • Support the delivery of the Asia Culture and Conduct Programme agenda by driving initiatives and being key contact person for market champions.

Requirements

  • Experience in regulatory risk and controls; preferable background in Audit, Regulatory Compliance/ Financial Crime Risk or other Business Management roles.
  • Good analytical skill with ability to understand and interpret complex regulatory requirements and translate into business requirements.
  • Well-developed leadership skills, not just at a team level but able to engage and drive at all levels, internally and externally.
  • Good communication skills, with ability to summarise complex topics concisely both verbally and in writing.
  • Good understanding of the regulatory landscape impacting the banking industry.
  • Detailed knowledge of how the organisation fits together across Global Businesses and Global Functions, and the ability to mobilise established networks to get things done.
  • Ability to drive the agenda, influence and communicate at all levels of the organisation.
  • Good understanding of customer segments/ financial services/ products across the WPB markets is preferable.
  • Self-starter, comfortable working with concepts, ambiguity and on their own initiative.
  • Broad experience of major programme or cross market/ region project management.

Candidate with less relevant experience or skills may be offered a lower Global Career Band than stated above.

Due to the urgent hiring need, candidates with immediate right to work locally and no relocation need will be prioritised.

You’ll achieve more when you join HSBC.

We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment. Job Summary

As a Relationship Manager, you'll be responsible for managing and developing relationships with clients of Priority Banking & Priority Private Banking to drive business growth and meet the bank's strategic objectives. You’ll help clients set wealth goals, manage investments, and create portfolios for long-term growth and stability. You’ll be supported by specialists in the areas of investment, insurance, products and treasury to provide clients with comprehensive solutions.

This is an opportunity for you to demonstrate your relationship management, sales, customer service and communications skills. Our Relationship Managers can advance their careers across client segments or explore roles across Wealth and Retail Banking.

About Our Wealth And Retail Banking Business

We service more than 13 million individuals and small businesses, with a focus on the affluent segment which encompasses Private Banking, Priority Private, Priority Banking, and Premium. In the mass retail space, we're focused on emerging affluent clients who will progress in their wealth journey with us and form the pipeline of future affluent clients.

We’re a leading wealth manager in Asia, Africa and the Middle East, and our deep local presence and international network enables us to capture the strong structural tailwinds which are driving cross-border wealth flows. Our comprehensive product propositions span across deposits, payments, financing, advisory, investments and bancassurance.

We’re investing USD $1.5 billion in our Affluent banking business. Our investment focuses on affluent frontline teams, wealth and digital platforms, and client centres, as well as brand and marketing, to drive growth. You’ll join a growing franchise within Standard Chartered Group.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support our clients to meet their financial needs, as they progress through their career and life-stages.
  • Build relationships for the long-term and understand clients’ financial needs and aspirations to grow, manage and protect their wealth, with appropriate investment solutions.
  • Stay ahead of the market and get regular market updates and investment insights from our Chief Investment Office (CIO) to share with clients.
  • Leverage myWealth digital and help clients to create custom portfolios, check performance and asset allocation based on CIO’s advice.
  • Provide outstanding client experiences.

Skills And Experience

  • Financial skills
  • Analytical skills

Qualifications

  • A minimum of 2 years of experience in client acquisition, relationship management and retail banking.
  • Technical knowledge and expertise in consumer banking products (i.e. Treasury, Equities, Funds, Insurance, etc.).
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal and relationship building skills.
  • Self-starter and team player who enjoys working in an international environment.
  • Local language skills, client networks and experience.

About Standard Chartered

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What We Offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

  • University degree in related disciplines

Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

Job Description

Job Summary

  • Conduct investigations into concerns allegations or risk events involving criminal conduct, dishonesty or deliberate breaches of policies or regulations.
  • Ensure investigations align with relevant laws, regulations, and Group standards, including escalation, case management, data capture, evidence management, electronic evidence review, reporting, interviewing, and attending internal disciplinary panels.
  • Prioritize multiple investigations, tasks, projects, and responsibilities while maintaining positive stakeholder relationships.
  • Keep relevant stakeholders and appropriate senior management informed of relevant investigative developments.
  • Assist in regulatory and government investigations, including data source identification and extraction.
  • Develop and disseminate data analytics, providing relevant management information to stakeholders.
  • Maintain relationships with law enforcement and coordinate the provision of responses to search warrants, local production orders, court orders, request for information from regulators or law enforcement agencies, and attend Court as required.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy

  • To manage the conduct of appropriate investigations in order to minimise financial losses, reputational and regulatory risks, and operational risk events involving criminal conduct, dishonesty or deliberate breaches of policies or regulations.

Business

  • Provide reports and other Management Information in agreed and standardised format.
  • Coordinate identification of themes, trends and lessons learnt from investigations in China to support the continuous improvement of the Bank’s conduct and control environment.

Processes

  • Conduct and manage non-government investigations against the Bank and/or with employees that have potential material impact on the Bank from either a reputational, regulatory, financial or litigation perspective (or any combination of the same).
  • As required, investigate data leakage cases escalated for China and assist in promoting awareness of the importance of confidentiality of bank information. Support management and promote Speaking Up in country with assistance from Regional investigative team.
  • Adopt a flexible approach in supporting other areas within the Group Investigations structure (and in seeking inbound support when necessary) to promote effective and efficient allocation of investigative resources.

People & Talent

  • Establish, develop and maintain close collaboration with key internal functional stakeholders. including Legal, Compliance, Audit, Risk, FCC and HR, to fully embed the Group Investigations framework including the formalisation of policies, procedures, processes and controls.

Risk Management

  • Maintain close interaction with those Risk Owners to whom responsibility is delegated to ensure resolution of system and control improvements identified through the Group Investigations process. Ensure Head, Shared Investigative Services, China, is fully informed of all key risks and issues in area of responsibility and reported in line with Bank’s operational risk process.

Governance

  • Reinforce an effective and exemplary risk and control culture and further strengthen the control environment.
  • Act to minimise operational loss and audit failures and take proactive measures to respond to matters arising.

Regulatory & Business Conduct

  • Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
  • Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.
  • Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters.

Key Stakeholders

  • Business and function representatives
  • HR
  • Compliance
  • Legal
  • Financial Crime Compliance
  • Audit
  • Risk

Skills and Experience

  • Interview
  • Investigation

Qualifications

Required

  • 8-10 years investigative, compliance, intelligence, consulting or audit experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to run end-to-end investigations, audits or relevant reviews.
  • Excellent communication skills.
  • Relevant degree holder, or comparable experience.
  • Native speaker fluency in Mandarin.
  • Business proficient English language speaking and writing skills.
  • Excellent judgement. Excellent collaborative and team playing skills. Diplomacy, empathy and a ‘can-do attitude’. Politeness, sensitivity and the ability to gently, but professionally stand your ground when needed.
  • An inquisitive approach to practices, procedures and specific transactions. Personal authority and integrity. Independence, creativity, resourcefulness and resilience.
  • Must possess ability to assess risk, strong leadership qualities, excellent interpersonal skills and multi-cultural awareness and sensitivity.

Desirable

  • Knowledge of banking systems.
  • Knowledge of law enforcement practices.

About Standard Chartered

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What we offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

Profile Description

Standard Chartered Bank

Description:

Citi Research delivers industry-leading investment analysis to Citi’s global institutional investor and wealth management client base. Our team includes some 350 publishing analysts globally, with fundamental coverage of ~3,600 equity securities, as well as areas such as quantitative analysis, economics, fixed-income/rates/credit, FX, commodities, and data analytics. We also deliver access services such as conferences & events, corporate access & visits, and direct insights from market, policy, and industry experts.

Citi Research is seeking a Supervisory Analyst / Editor / Designated Quality Review Officer (DQRO) to join our nascent Shanghai-based Research office under Citigroup Securities (China) Co. Ltd. This is a role for a seasoned professional combining responsibilities in editorial, risk management, and operational processes. This role will primarily support and review research product produced by our new Shanghai team, both in English and Chinese. The role may also involve some review of global ex-PRC research product. The role requires strong editorial skills and financial/investment topics comprehension in order to filter, prioritize and validate potentially complex and dynamic material from multiple sources. Strong communication and diplomacy skills are required. Attention to detail is a must!

Key Responsibilities:

  • Review investment research product to ensure compliance with PRC and US FINRA regulations, including reasonable basis and sourcing requirements.
  • Review investment research product to ensure compliance with Citi’s internal research content guidelines, as detailed in our research guidebooks and policies.
  • Edit investment research for quality, clarity, commerciality, style, and grammar.
  • Review both Chinese and English variants, including cross-checking consistency.
  • Review investment research language/tone and content for franchise risk, with consideration of the firm's reputation and business exposures, and in light of PRC and global political and client sensitivities. Be capable of editing to mitigate such risks (while maintaining our independent views), as well as determining when escalation is appropriate.
  • Handle the checking of investment research product for 1) issuer mentions for cross-checking against our Watch List; 2) the inclusion of appropriate disclaimers & disclosures; 3) data consistency; and 4) distribution tagging and other product & template elements.
  • Act as an editorial project manager, providing end-to-end traffic management of work-in-progress, liaising as needed with analyst teams, other Publications staff, product managers, control & compliance teams, data and technical support teams, and other relevant partners, to resolve problems and ensure product ultimately publishes.
  • Broadly as a Citi staffer, assess risk appropriately when business decisions are made, work in compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to policies, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency.

Qualifications:

  • Have passed the examination uniformly organized by the CSRC for securities business personnel; Securities Association of China (SAC) test.
  • Holding a FINRA Series-16 license is a major advantage. We may also consider strong candidates without Series-16 and would sponsor them to sit the exam, including providing study materials. Quick study prep time and then successfully passing this challenging exam is a requirement for the role.
  • Candidate should have at least five years of experience creating, supporting, or editing investment/financial analytic content. Candidate should be a fluent Chinese and English speaker with evidence of editorial and writing capability.
  • We expect candidates to have strong familiarity with financial markets, financial terminology, and ongoing business news in PRC, Asia, and globally.
  • Ability to prioritize and to juggle multiple tasks simultaneously amid tight deadlines.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to exercise sound and balanced judgment.
  • Meticulous and detail oriented. Key aspects of the role involve being able to remember and apply many guidelines and procedures on a consistent and reliable basis.
  • Team members should have comfort working with sometimes complex publishing software platforms (e.g. Sinitek) and ability to coordinate with partner teams when trouble-shooting technical issues.
  • Team player with good interpersonal skills, and the patience and diplomacy to work with demanding internal customers and effectively find win-win solutions.

This job description provides a high-level review of the types of work performed. Other job-related duties may be assigned as required.

Other Key Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s undergraduate university degree or higher
  • PRC nationality
  • Have complete civil capacity; be of good moral character, fair-minded and honest, and possess sound professional ethics.
  • Have not incurred any criminal penalty or any serious administrative penalty related to securities or futures business.

Corporate and Institutional Banking

HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking is a markets-led, financing-focused business that provides investment and financial solutions. Through our international network, we connect emerging and mature markets, covering key growth areas. We partner with our corporate, government and institutional clients to help them achieve consistent, long-term performance. Our products and services include advisory, financing, prime services, research and analysis, securities services, trading and sales and transaction banking.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team.

In This Role, You Will

Impact on the Business/Function:

  • Support the execution of the Outbound strategy, including strategy paper, initiatives formulation, driving actions and track the deliverables.
  • Help drive the in-country execution of the Group's Outbound strategy to deliver revenues and achieve the Annual Operating Plan (AOP) targets.
  • Support customer account strategies and liaise with Regions/Branches assigning prospects and opportunities to HBCN Coverage Banker/Global Network Banking (GNB) RMs.
  • Develop metrics and reporting mechanisms that monitor execution of the Outbound strategy.
  • Interpret and communicate any global GNB and regulatory developments and ensure timely training and familiarization for frontline teams is delivered.
  • Support the execution of tactical projects to ensure that market firsts are attained for key products and market trends.
  • Work on strategy papers and presentations to raise Outbound and international awareness/knowledge for front-line colleagues.

Customers / Stakeholders

  • Build working level relationships with trade bodies, business councils and commercial chambers. Support capturing ODI opportunities.
  • Participate in meetings with Outbound clients and prospects, to provide guidance, pitch for new business, resolve any issues, and facilitate smooth operations and services, thus building loyalty and client satisfaction.
  • Help establish the agenda for internal education (e.g. workshops and seminars) and external marketing (client forums and summits).
  • Deepen customer relationships through championing business co-operation with key stakeholders including Global Business, Global Products and Global Functions, to contribute to Outbound strategy.
  • Support with planning workshops, forums, seminars, roadshows and presentations.
  • Work with in-country stakeholders where required to remove any blockages for transactions and coordinate escalation to resolve matters in a timely and efficient manner.

Leadership & Teamwork

  • Work closely with Global Businesses, Global Products and Global Functions to support on preparing content, papers and presentations related to execution of a comprehensive strategy for the China Outbound proposition.

Job Description

Asset Management

A career with Goldman Sachs Asset Management is an opportunity to help clients across the globe realize their potential, while you discover your own. As part of one of the world’s leading asset managers with over $2 trillion in assets under supervision, you can expect to participate in exciting investment opportunities while collaborating with talented colleagues from all asset classes and regions, and building meaningful relationships with your clients. Working in a culture that values integrity and transparency, you will be part of a diverse team that is passionate about our craft, our clients, and building sustainable success. Bringing together traditional and alternative investments, Goldman Sachs Asset Management provides clients around the world with a dedicated partnership and focus on long-term performance. As primary investment area within Goldman Sachs, we provide investment and advisory services for pension plans, sovereign wealth funds, insurance companies, endowments, foundations, financial advisors and individuals.

External Investing Group (XIG)

The External Investing Group (XIG) is one of the world's largest and most active private markets investing platforms, deploying capital across private equity funds, co-investments, secondaries, continuation vehicles, GP stakes, private credit, hedge funds and special situations. XIG maintains longstanding relationships with many of the world's leading investment managers and has privileged access to many of the most attractive opportunities in alternatives. The platform is fundamentally focused on identifying differentiated investments, underwriting assets and executing transactions across the private markets ecosystem.

Investment professionals at XIG are responsible for sourcing opportunities, conducting company-level due diligence, building financial models, assessing management teams, structuring and negotiating transactions, and constructing portfolios across a broad range of strategies. Rather than investing through a single lens, XIG participates across multiple levels of the private markets value chain, including direct investments in companies through co-investments, secondary acquisitions of private equity fund interests, continuation vehicle transactions, and strategic ownership stakes in alternative asset management firms.

With more than 400 professionals across 12 global offices and almost $600 billion of client assets, XIG combines the scale and resources of a leading global asset manager with a highly selective investment process. As one of the broadest, deepest and longest-standing open-architecture platforms globally, XIG manages both customized and commingled solutions while evaluating thousands of investment opportunities annually. Investment teams work directly with sponsors, portfolio companies and management teams across buyouts, growth equity, venture capital, private credit and opportunistic investments, frequently accessing proprietary, capacity-constrained or otherwise difficult-to-source transactions. Investors access these capabilities through primary fund commitments, secondary investments, co-investments and other solutions designed for institutional and ultra-high-net-worth clients.

For candidates considering careers in private markets, XIG offers a differentiated opportunity at the intersection of direct investing and alternatives. The platform combines the analytical rigor and asset-level underwriting experience associated with leading private equity firms with exposure to a broad range of transaction types and investment strategies. Professionals engage with senior investment partners across many of the world's leading private market institutions while developing expertise in company analysis, valuation, transaction execution, portfolio construction and manager assessment. As a result, XIG investment professionals build a highly transferable investing toolkit while participating in some of the largest and most innovative segments of the alternatives industry.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct due diligence and evaluate private equity opportunities; secondary private equity transactions, with a specific focus on asset-level valuation within portfolios or continuation vehicles; primary fund commitments for a variety of private market strategies; co-investment opportunities across a broad range of deal types and sectors
  • Support the deal team on direct investment opportunities (single asset secondaries, co-investments) by evaluating financial, legal and commercial due diligence materials and building operating and buyout models in various asset classes, meeting with management and GPs
  • Perform due diligence on private market fund managers across Asia-Pacific, including assessing the quality of investment teams, investment strategies, alignment and track record
  • Present investment opportunities to the Investment Committee through written and oral presentations, and conduct required follow-ups
  • Coordinate the execution of investments across all deal types, including working closely with internal (e.g., internal counsel, compliance, cash management) and external parties (e.g., private equity managers, external counsel)
  • Monitor the performance and risk profile of existing portfolio investments

Qualifications

  • 3-7 years of experience in Corporate Finance/ M&A/ Leverage Finance/ Private Equity/ Other Private Markets Investing in Asia-Pacific; position will be commensurate with experience
  • Proven academic performance with a degree from a top university; MBA a plus for more senior positions
  • Excellent modeling, analytical, communication and interpersonal skills
  • Strong organizational skills to oversee production of a high volume of quality work within tight timeframes, often including multiple simultaneous projects
  • Attention to detail – proven experience of delivering high levels of accuracy
  • Candidate must be a team player, self-motivated and demonstrate a willingness to take on responsibility
  • Knowledge and understanding of Excel, PowerPoint and Word and adaptability to other software products

Written and verbal communication skills in English. A second language (Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, etc, will be strongly preferred).

About Goldman Sachs

At Goldman Sachs, we commit our people, capital and ideas to help our clients, shareholders and the communities we serve to grow. Founded in 1869, we are a leading global investment banking, securities and investment management firm. Headquartered in New York, we maintain offices around the world.

We believe who you are makes you better at what you do. We're committed to fostering and advancing diversity and inclusion in our own workplace and beyond by ensuring every individual within our firm has a number of opportunities to grow professionally and personally, from our training and development opportunities and firmwide networks to benefits, wellness and personal finance offerings and mindfulness programs. Learn more about our culture, benefits, and people at GS.com/careers .

We're committed to finding reasonable accommodations for candidates with special needs or disabilities during our recruiting process. Learn more: https://www.goldmansachs.com/careers/footer/disability-statement.html

© The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc., 2025. All rights reserved.

Goldman Sachs is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, veterans status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Job Description

Job Summary

Internal Audit strengthens the Bank's governance, risk management and control environment by providing independent assurance over the effectiveness of business activities, processes and controls.

The role enables informed decision-making through objective assessment of risks, controls and regulatory obligations, ensuring potential issues are identified, escalated and addressed appropriately. It supports organisational resilience by delivering assurance, insight and challenge that helps the Bank manage risk effectively while maintaining high standards of governance and accountability.

Key Responsibilities

Audit Assurance & Independent Challenge

  • Strengthen confidence in the Bank's governance, risk management and control environment through the delivery of independent, risk-based assurance activities.
  • Improve management understanding of control effectiveness by identifying control weaknesses, emerging risks and opportunities for improvement.
  • Enhance organisational accountability by providing objective challenge and evidence-based conclusions on key risk and control matters.
  • Support informed decision-making through timely audit observations, recommendations and assurance outcomes.

Risk, Control & Governance Assessment

  • Improve the Bank's ability to manage risk by evaluating the design and effectiveness of governance arrangements, processes and control frameworks.
  • Strengthen the control environment through the identification and assessment of operational, financial, regulatory, conduct and technology-related risks.
  • Enhance visibility of control weaknesses, emerging risks and governance concerns through structured assessment and reporting activities.
  • Support sustainable risk management by evaluating whether remediation actions effectively address identified issues.

Audit Delivery & Quality Excellence

  • Deliver high-quality audit outcomes through the consistent application of Internal Audit methodology, professional standards and quality requirements.
  • Improve audit effectiveness by maintaining robust planning, testing, documentation and evidence-management practices.
  • Enhance confidence in audit conclusions through objective analysis, professional judgement and fact-based assessment.
  • Support continuous improvement of audit practices, tools and methodologies to strengthen audit quality and efficiency.

Skills and Experience

Priority Skills

  • Data Analytics and Insights: Use audit and investigations data to confidently detect anomalies, test hypotheses, identify patterns, and transform evidence into clear forward-looking insights that strengthen scoping, findings, and stakeholder decisions-making.
  • Human and AI Collaboration: Apply AI responsibly to enhance audit & investigation workstreams like research, pattern recognition, documentation and synthesis while maintaining professional judgment, skepticism, confidentiality, and appropriate challenge to validate outputs and decisions
  • Strategic and Proactive Mindset: Anticipate future needs, see beyond tasks and compliance requirements, recognize patterns across engagements, and detect systemic risks early.
  • Relationship Management and Communication: Communicate effectively with auditees, case stakeholders and senior leaders; ask incisive questions; handle difficult conversations well; and convey complex evidence clearly. Proactively build and sustain relationships to stay informed and improve audit planning
  • Resilience and Adaptability: Adapts and remains effective in the face of change and pressure by showing resilience persevering through challenges and recover quickly from setbacks

Other Skills

  • Internal Audit: Internal Audit skill involves evaluating and improving the effectiveness of risk management, control, and governance processes within an organization. Key responsibilities include assessing compliance with financial laws and regulations, and examining internal processes to ensure they are efficient and error-free. A distinctive feature of this skill is its dual focus on assurance and advisory services, which helps organizations not only identify weaknesses but also enhance operational efficiencies.
  • Audit Analytics: Audit Analytics involves the use of data analysis techniques to enhance audit processes, focusing on the evaluation of financial records and transactions for accuracy and compliance. Key responsibilities include identifying risk areas and ensuring regulatory compliance through detailed data assessments. Its distinctive feature is the application of sophisticated analytical tools and techniques to extract actionable insights from large datasets, significantly improving audit efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Compliance Audit: Compliance Audit involves evaluating the adherence of an organization to regulatory guidelines and internal policies. Key responsibilities involve the systematic review of procedures, controls, and operations. Its distinctive characteristic is the emphasis on preventative measures and mitigating risks, ensuring organizations operate within the legal frameworks and industry standards.
  • Audit Finding: Audit Finding involves the identification and documentation of issues uncovered during an audit. Key responsibilities include evaluating compliance with regulations and assessing the adequacy of internal controls. A distinctive feature of this skill is its critical role in enhancing transparency and accountability in organizational processes.
  • Integrity Management: Integrity Management focuses on ensuring ethical practices and moral soundness across an organization's operations. Key responsibilities include establishing ethical guidelines and resolving ethical dilemmas effectively. Its distinctive feature is promoting a trustworthy and transparent work environment, crucial for sustaining long-term organizational success.

Motivations

  • Motivated by understanding how organisations manage risk and identifying opportunities to strengthen governance, controls and decision-making.
  • Energised by analysing complex information, evaluating evidence and providing objective conclusions on important business and risk matters.
  • Enjoy applying professional judgement and independent challenge to improve organisational effectiveness, accountability and resilience.
  • Find satisfaction in working across diverse business areas, building trusted relationships and influencing positive risk and control outcomes.

Qualifications

  • Experience assessing risks, controls, governance arrangements or business processes within audit, risk, compliance, financial services or related environments.
  • Experience performing reviews, testing, analysis or assurance activities to evaluate control effectiveness and identify areas for improvement.
  • Experience gathering, interpreting and assessing information from multiple sources to support evidence-based conclusions and recommendations.
  • Experience preparing reports, observations or management insights that communicate risks, issues and findings in a clear and structured manner.
  • Experience engaging with business, risk and control stakeholders to understand operational activities, challenges and control environments
  • Business English

About Standard Chartered

We're a global bank connecting clients to our differentiated network, offering growth opportunities in the world's most dynamic markets. Our strategy, which combines cross-border capabilities and leading wealth management expertise, helps us deliver our purpose - to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity.

Over our 170-year history, and across a unique geographical footprint connecting Asia, Africa and the Middle East to each other and the world, we've built a bank like no other, with diverse capabilities and partnerships that set us apart.

What We Offer

  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions, and geographies.
  • In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.
  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global employee assistance programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and self-help toolkits.
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual, and digital learning.

Visit our careers website to learn more about us: www.sc.com/careers.

  • Effective communication and collaboration skills.
  • Ownership mindset with a willingness to learn and contribute to continuous improvement.

Who We Are Looking For

The Alpha Portfolio Services team is a dedicated global business team working with Clients, SSC IT, client service, and the business operations teams to ensure accurate end-to-end oversight of Information Delivery to our clients. The Alpha Portfolio Services team is responsible for ensuring the Investment book of records is accurately maintained and ensuring accurate client portfolios are reflected on State Street platforms. The role will interact with the Clients (predominantly Front Office) and being a key liaison with various portfolio managers and internal SSC parties in identifying an issue as well as managing that a suitable resolution is found and communicated to the Client. The role will need to initiate and develop good communication and interpersonal relationship with business operations teams and IT and to maintain the high level of service that is currently being provided to all the clients.

Why this role is important to us

The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Global Services (SSGS). SSGS gives asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGS’ tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.

Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As Senior Associate, you will

  • Ensure client queries relating to the Recordkeeping system and client file deliveries are tracked, with proactive management to ensure timely response and resolution
  • Perform daily checks on file deliverables to the clients, investigate and report discrepancies and ensure daily resolution of identified queries
  • Provide Subject Matter expertise for complex system architecture queries/changes
  • Perform an overview function for the Shared Services functions identifying operational trends, issues and areas for improvement.
  • Perform work independently within scope of established guidelines and according to specific procedures.
  • Investigate and resolve operational and various IT issues (e.g. Asset servicing, Trade Operations, Client Reporting)
  • Support and provide analysis for Client Change Request items impacting the Enterprise processes and Operating Models
  • Work independently to research and resolve problems considering multiple avenues for resolution. Trouble shoot issues and provide resolutions to various impacted teams
  • Communicate effectively on issues / problems to the Client and to SSC management and ensure a proper and timely follow-up to ensure resolution.
  • Provide guidance, support, act as resource and assist team members from multiple operational areas relating to Enterprise queries
  • Complete any ad-hoc tasks as identified by the line manager


What We Value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

  • Portfolio Valuations reconciliations/Investigations experience is required. Candidates should be able to validate portfolio movements day over day and highlight any issues.
  • Excellent technical ability, Excellent analytical skills are essential for this role.
  • Strong communication (especially written) and presentation skills to audiences of different sizes and levels of seniority.
  • Must be self-motivated, adaptable and show initiative in different circumstances and under pressure
  • Extensive asset management experience, including investment operations


Education & Preferred Qualifications

  • Degree in finance, business, technology or equivalent or relevant industry experience of 3-5 years
  • Experience in writing SQL, Oracle, Sybase is a plus
  • Strong MS Excel, Access, Word, Powerpoint skills necessary
  • Strong English written and spoken ability
